verses.1:1: In the days of one judge, when the judges were in authority, a famine arose in the land. And a man departed from Bethlehem of Judah to sojourn in the region of Moab with his wife and two children.
verses.1:2: He was called Elimelech, and his wife Naomi, and two sons, one Mahlon and the other Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. And entering the region of Moab, they stayed there.
verses.1:3: And Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died, and she herself was left with her sons.
verses.1:4: They took Moabite wives, one of whom was called Orpah, and the other Ruth. And they remained there for ten years,
verses.1:5: and both died, namely Mahlon and Chilion; and the woman was left bereft of her two children and her husband.
verses.1:6: And she arose to go to her homeland with both of her daughters-in-law from the region of Moab, for she had heard that the Lord had looked upon His people and had given them food.
verses.1:7: Therefore she went out from the place of her sojourning with both daughters-in-law, and now set on the road to return to the land of Judah,
verses.1:8: she said to them, "Go to the house of your mother. May the Lord show mercy to you, just as you have done with the dead and with me.
verses.1:9: May He grant you to find rest in the houses of the husbands whom you are going to obtain." And she kissed them. And raising their voices, they began to weep,
verses.1:10: and to say, "We will go with you to your people."
verses.1:11: She answered them, "Return, my daughters; why do you come with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, so that you could hope for husbands from me?
verses.1:12: Return, my daughters, and depart, for I am already worn out with old age and not fit for the bond of marriage. Even if I were able to conceive tonight and bear sons,
verses.1:13: if you were willing to wait for them until they grow up and complete the years of maturity, you will be old women before you marry. Do not do so, I beg you, my daughters, because your distress presses upon me more, and the hand of the Lord has gone out against me."
verses.1:14: Therefore, raising their voices, they began to weep again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned, while Ruth clung to her mother-in-law,
verses.1:15: and Naomi said to her, "Look, your relative has returned to her people and to her gods; go with her."
verses.1:16: She answered, "Do not oppose me so that I leave you and depart; for wherever you go, I will go, and where you stay, I likewise will stay. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.
verses.1:17: Whatever land receives you as you die, in it I will die, and there I will receive a place of burial. May the Lord do these things to me, and add these things, unless death alone separates me and you."
verses.1:18: Seeing, therefore, that Ruth had resolved with a steadfast mind to go with her, Naomi was unwilling to oppose her, nor any longer to persuade her to return to her own people;
verses.1:19: and they set out together and came to Bethlehem. When they had entered the city, a swift report spread widely among everyone, and the women were saying, "This is that Naomi."
verses.1:20: She said to them, "Do not call me Naomi (that is, beautiful), but call me Mara (that is, bitter), because the Almighty has greatly filled me with bitterness.
verses.1:21: I went out full, and the Lord has brought me back empty. Why then do you call me Naomi, whom the Lord has humbled and the Almighty has afflicted?"
verses.1:22: Therefore Naomi came with Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, from the land of her sojourning, and returned to Bethlehem when the barley was first being reaped.
verses.2:1: Now her husband Elimelech had a blood relative, a powerful man of great wealth, named Boaz.
verses.2:2: And Ruth the Moabite said to her mother-in-law, "If you command, I will go into the field and gather the ears of grain that escape the hands of the reapers, wherever I find the favor of a master of a household who is kind toward me." She answered her, "Go, my daughter."
verses.2:3: So she departed and was gathering ears of grain behind the reapers. Now it happened that the field had an owner named Boaz, who was of the kin of Elimelech.
verses.2:4: And look, he himself was coming from Bethlehem, and he said to the reapers, "The Lord be with you." And they answered him, "May the Lord bless you."
verses.2:5: And Boaz said to the young man who was in charge of the reapers, "Whose young woman is this?"
verses.2:6: He answered him, "This is the Moabite woman who came with Naomi from the region of Moab,
verses.2:7: and she asked to gather the remaining ears of grain, following the footsteps of the reapers; and from morning until now she has been standing in the field, and she has not returned home even for a moment."
verses.2:8: And Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen, daughter, do not go into another field to gather, nor depart from this place, but join yourself to my young women,
verses.2:9: and where they reap, follow. For I have instructed my servants that no one is to trouble you; and also if you grow thirsty, go to the packs and drink the water from which the servants also drink."
verses.2:10: Falling on her face and bowing down upon the ground, she said to him, "How has this come to me, that I should find favor before your eyes, and that you would deign to acknowledge me, a foreign woman?"
verses.2:11: He answered her, "Everything that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband has been reported to me, and that you left your parents and the land in which you were born, and came to a people whom you did not know before.
verses.2:12: May the Lord repay you for your work, and may you receive a full reward from the Lord God of Israel, to whom you have come, and under whose wings you have taken refuge."
verses.2:13: She said, "I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, since you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your maidservant, though I am not like one of your young women."
verses.2:14: And Boaz said to her, "When the hour for eating comes, come here, and eat bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." So she sat at the side of the reapers, and heaped up roasted grain for herself, and ate and was satisfied, and took the leftovers.
verses.2:15: And she arose from there to gather ears of grain as usual. Now Boaz commanded his servants, saying, "Even if she wants to reap with you, do not forbid her;
verses.2:16: and also drop some from your own sheaves on purpose, and allow them to remain, so that she may gather without embarrassment, and let no one rebuke her as she gathers."
verses.2:17: So she gathered in the field until evening, and beating and shaking out with a stick what she had gathered, she found about the measure of an ephah of barley, that is, three modii.
verses.2:18: Carrying these, she returned to the city and showed them to her mother-in-law; moreover, she brought out and gave her some of the leftovers of her food with which she had been satisfied.
verses.2:19: And her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you gather today, and where did you do your work? Blessed be the one who has had mercy on you." And she told her with whom she had worked, and told her the name of the man, that he was called Boaz.
verses.2:20: Naomi answered her, "May he be blessed by the Lord, because the same favor that he had shown to the living he has kept also for the dead." And again she said, "The man is our close relative."
verses.2:21: And Ruth said, "He also commanded me this, that I should stay joined to his reapers until all the crops are reaped."
verses.2:22: Her mother-in-law said to her, "It is better, my daughter, that you go out with his young women to reap, so that no one in another's field may oppose you."
verses.2:23: So she joined herself to the young women of Boaz, and reaped with them until the barley and the wheat were stored in the granaries.
verses.3:1: Now after she had returned to her mother-in-law, she heard from her, "My daughter, I will seek rest for you, and I will provide so that it may go well for you.
verses.3:2: This Boaz, whose young women you joined in the field, is our close relative, and tonight he is winnowing the barley threshing floor.
verses.3:3: Therefore, wash yourself, and anoint yourself, and put on finer garments, and go down to the threshing floor; do not let the man see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
verses.3:4: Now when he goes to sleep, note the place in which he sleeps; and you will come and uncover the cloak with which he is covered at his feet, and lay yourself down, and lie there; and he himself will say what you ought to do."
verses.3:5: She answered, "Whatever you command, I will do."
verses.3:6: And she went down to the threshing floor and did everything that her mother-in-law had ordered her.
verses.3:7: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk and had become quite cheerful, and had gone to sleep beside the heap of sheaves, she came secretly, and uncovering the cloak, she laid herself down at his feet.
verses.3:8: And look, already in the middle of the night the man was startled and troubled, and he saw a woman lying at his feet,
verses.3:9: and he said to her, "Who are you?" And she answered, "I am Ruth, your maidservant. Spread your cloak over your servant, because you are a close relative."
verses.3:10: And he said, "You are blessed by the Lord, daughter, and you have surpassed your earlier mercy with the later, because you have not followed young men, whether poor or rich.
verses.3:11: Therefore do not be afraid, but whatever you say to me, I will do for you. For all the people who live within the gates of my city know that you are a woman of virtue.
verses.3:12: Nor do I deny that I am a close relative, but there is another closer than I am.
verses.3:13: Rest tonight, and when morning comes, if he is willing to keep you by right of close kinship, the matter is well settled; but if he is unwilling, I myself will take you without any doubt, as the Lord lives. Sleep until morning."
verses.3:14: So she slept at his feet until the passing of the night. She arose, therefore, before people could recognize one another, and Boaz said, "Take care that no one knows that you came here."
verses.3:15: And again he said, "Spread out your cloak with which you cover yourself, and hold it with both hands." As she stretched it out and held it, he measured out six modii of barley and placed it upon her. Carrying it, she entered the city,
verses.3:16: and came to her mother-in-law. She said to her, "What have you done, daughter?" And she recounted to her everything that the man had done for her.
verses.3:17: And she said, "Look, he gave me six modii of barley, and he said, 'I do not want you to return empty to your mother-in-law.'"
verses.3:18: And Naomi said, "Wait, daughter, until we see what outcome the matter has, for the man will not rest until he has completed what he has spoken."
verses.4:1: Boaz therefore went up to the gate and sat down there. And when he saw the close relative passing by, about whom mention had been made earlier, he said to him, "Turn aside for a little while and sit down here," calling him by his name. And he turned aside and sat down.
verses.4:2: Then Boaz, taking ten men from the elders of the city, said to them, "Sit down here."
verses.4:3: When they were seated, he spoke to the close relative, "Naomi, who has returned from the region of Moab, will sell the portion of our brother Elimelech's field;
verses.4:4: this I wanted you to hear, and I wanted to tell it to you in the presence of all those seated and of the elders of my people. If you wish to possess it by right of kinship, buy it and possess it; but if it does not please you, inform me of this very thing, so that I may know what I must do, for there is no close relative except you, who are first, and me, who am second." And he answered, "I will buy the field."
verses.4:5: Boaz said to him, "When you buy the field from the hand of the woman, you must also take Ruth the Moabite, who was the wife of the deceased, so that you may raise up the name of your close relative in his inheritance."
verses.4:6: He answered, "I relinquish the right of kinship, for I must not wipe out the posterity of my family; you use my privilege, which I declare that I willingly forgo."
verses.4:7: Now this was the custom in former times in Israel among close relatives, that whenever one relinquished his right to another, so that the concession would be binding, a man would untie his sandal and give it to his neighbor; this was the testimony of relinquishment in Israel.
verses.4:8: Boaz therefore said to his close relative, "Take off your sandal." And immediately he untied it from his foot.
verses.4:9: Then he said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have taken possession of all that belonged to Elimelech and Chilion and Mahlon, with Naomi handing it over,
verses.4:10: and have taken Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, in marriage, in order that I may raise up the name of the deceased in his inheritance, so that his name may not be wiped out from his family and brothers and people. You, I say, are witnesses of this matter."
verses.4:11: All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, answered, "We are witnesses. May the Lord make this woman, who is entering your house, like Rachel and Leah, who built the house of Israel, so that she may be an example of virtue in Ephrathah and may have a renowned name in Bethlehem;
verses.4:12: and may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the offspring that the Lord will give you by this young woman."
verses.4:13: So Boaz took Ruth and received her as his wife, and he went in to her, and the Lord granted her to conceive and bear a son.
verses.4:14: And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the Lord, who has not allowed a successor of your family to be lacking; and may his name be called in Israel,
verses.4:15: and may you have one who will comfort your soul and nourish your old age, for he has been born of your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is much better to you than if you had seven sons."
verses.4:16: And taking up the boy, Naomi placed him in her bosom, and she performed the duty of a nurse and of one who carried him.
verses.4:17: Now the woman's female neighbors, congratulating her and saying, "A son has been born to Naomi," called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.4:18: These are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron;
verses.4:19: Hezron fathered Aram; Aram fathered Amminadab;
verses.4:20: Amminadab fathered Nahshon; Nahshon fathered Salmon;
verses.4:21: Salmon fathered Boaz; Boaz fathered Obed;
verses.4:22: Obed fathered Jesse; Jesse fathered David.

notes.1:1: The Vulgate uniquely specifies "in the days of one judge" (in diebus unius judicis) before adding "when the judges were in authority," whereas the Hebrew reads simply "in the days when the judges judged."
notes.1:13: The Vulgate renders this clause distinctly as "you will be old women before you marry" (ante eritis vetulae quam nubatis), whereas the Hebrew asks rhetorically whether they would refrain from marrying.
notes.1:17: The Vulgate expands the brief Hebrew "where you die, I will die" into the fuller expression "Whatever land receives you as you die, in it I will die, and there I will receive a place of burial."
notes.1:20: Jerome inserted the parenthetical etymological explanations "(that is, beautiful)" and "(that is, bitter)" directly into the Latin text; neither gloss appears in the Hebrew or Greek.
notes.2:7: Where the Hebrew of the final clause is difficult (often taken as "except resting a little in the shelter"), the Vulgate reads clearly "and she has not returned home even for a moment."
notes.2:14: Following the Latin grammar with no change of subject and the reflexive pronoun "sibi," the clause reads "she heaped up roasted grain for herself." Some interpreters take Late Latin "sibi" here with Boaz as the implied subject ("he heaped up roasted grain for her"), matching the Hebrew.
notes.2:17: The Vulgate adds the explanatory gloss "that is, three modii" (id est, tres modios) to interpret the Hebrew ephah; a Roman modius was a dry measure of roughly one peck (about 8.7 liters).
notes.2:20: The implied subject of "had shown ... has kept" is grammatically Boaz (the subject of "May he be blessed"), though as in the Hebrew it is also sometimes taken to refer to the Lord.
notes.3:10: The Clementine Latin text reads third-person "est secuta" ("she has not followed"), a known textual variant for second-person "es secuta" ("you have not followed"), which the surrounding second-person address ("superasti," "Noli," "dixeris") requires.
notes.3:13: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew kinsman-redeemer terminology in legal kinship terms ("by right of close kinship," propinquitatis jure) and adds the emphatic phrase "without any doubt" (absque ulla dubitatione).
notes.3:15: Where the Hebrew leaves the unit unnamed ("six of barley") and has a masculine verb ("he entered"), the Vulgate specifies "six modii of barley" and uses the feminine participle and verb ("Carrying it, she entered").
notes.3:16: Where the Hebrew asks literally "Who are you, my daughter?" (an idiom for "How did you fare?"), the Vulgate renders it directly as "What have you done, daughter?" (Quid egisti, filia?).
notes.4:1: The Vulgate narrates "calling him by his name" (vocans eum nomine suo), whereas the Hebrew places a placeholder expression ("so-and-so") inside Boaz's speech. Throughout this chapter, the Vulgate also uses propinquus ("close relative") and jus propinquitatis ("right of kinship") for the Hebrew kinsman-redeemer terminology.
notes.4:8: In the Vulgate, Boaz is the subject who tells his close relative, "Take off your sandal," and the relative immediately unties it; the Hebrew instead has the relative say to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself," before removing the sandal.
notes.4:11: The Vulgate applies the final two clauses in the third person to Ruth ("so that she may be an example of virtue... and may have a renowned name"), whereas the Hebrew addresses Boaz in the second person.
notes.4:17: The Clementine Vulgate reads Vicinae autem mulieris (genitive singular, "the woman's female neighbors") and adds congratulantes ei ("congratulating her"), where other Latin witnesses read mulieres ("the neighbor women") and the Hebrew lacks "congratulating her."
notes.4:19: The Vulgate preserves the name Aram (matching the Septuagint and the New Testament genealogies in Matthew 1:3-4 and Luke 3:33), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Ram.
